overall_summary: Bitcoin is under pressure from hawkish macro signals as strong jobs data lifts Fed hike odds, yields test 4.8 percent, and the dollar strengthens. Geopolitical risks are rising with Hormuz tensions, higher oil, and new tariffs, while whales sell into the 83k area. Heavy spot ETF inflows near a billion dollars provide partial support ahead of critical CPI and PPI prints this week.
key_points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs pull nearly $987M third week
Hot NFP lifts Fed hike odds toward 60%
Whales flip to net selling at $83k resistance
Hormuz fears push oil toward multi-month highs
CPI and PPI this week critical for FOMC

items.title: Liquid Network Hit by $320M White-Hat BTC Drain
items.summary: Blockstream's Liquid sidechain, used by exchanges for faster Bitcoin settlement, saw roughly 4,000 BTC about 320 million dollars pulled from its federation wallet after a bug in the Elements software let attackers mint and peg out unbacked L-BTC. The network paused bridges and deposits, exchanges froze L-BTC activity, and the actors calling themselves white hats say they will return most funds once the patch is verified across nodes. Traders should care because it hits confidence in Bitcoin sidechains and federation custody even though the base Bitcoin chain itself was untouched, and any delayed return or further bugs could weigh on related liquidity.
items.impact: Short-term infrastructure confidence hit with limited direct BTC price cascade

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Pull Nearly $987M for Third Week
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about 987 million dollars in net inflows last week, the third straight positive week, with BlackRock's IBIT leading at roughly 692 million. Friday's haul narrowed to 175 million and was concentrated in just IBIT and Fidelity as markets headed into the Labor Day close. This shows institutions are still adding even while price chopped below 80k, giving traders a clean demand signal that can absorb macro selling if the streak holds after the holiday.
items.impact: Supports bid and cushions downside if inflows persist into next sessions

items.title: Hot Jobs Data Lifts Fed Hike Odds, BTC Holds Near $79k
items.summary: August payrolls came in at 162,000, triple the forecast, pushing September Fed hike odds toward 58 percent and sending the two-year yield to a 52-week high. Bitcoin slipped under 1 percent to hold around 79,300 while equities sold off more cleanly and oil stayed elevated on U.S.-Iran tensions. Traders need to watch whether ETF flows and residual risk appetite keep absorbing the hawkish repricing ahead of CPI and the mid-month FOMC, or if higher-for-longer finally bites harder.
items.impact: Macro headwind that can cap rallies until rate path clarifies

items.title: Whales Flip to Net Selling at $83k Resistance Wall
items.summary: Glassnode data shows every major wallet cohort has shifted into net distribution for the first time since early June, with whales holding 1,000-plus BTC leading the selling as Bitcoin failed to clear the 83,000 dollar supply wall and slipped back under 80k. This follows months of accumulation near the summer lows. A potential 50-200 day golden cross later this week offers a counter-signal, but traders should treat the 83k zone as unresolved until buyers absorb the distribution or price confirms a break.
items.impact: Adds overhead supply that can stall upside until distribution clears

items.title: Capital B Buys $29M Bitcoin, Largest Purchase in a Year
items.summary: French listed Bitcoin treasury firm Capital B acquired 376 BTC for 25.3 million euros, about 29 million dollars, its biggest single buy in a year and lifting total holdings to 3,521 BTC. The purchase was funded by recent capital raises that included an investment from Blockstream's Adam Back. It is another corporate accumulation print at current levels and signals European treasury demand remains alive even as price consolidates.
items.impact: Modest positive flow and treasury-adoption signal

items.title: Coldcard Hacker Moves $7.7M of Stolen Bitcoin
items.summary: The operator behind the third wave of Coldcard hardware-wallet thefts has moved roughly 97 BTC, about 7.7 million dollars or 45 percent of that wave's haul, partly through CoinJoin and earlier THORChain swaps. Galaxy Research says the broader exploit drained well over 1,700 BTC from weak-entropy seeds, with most funds still parked. Self-custody traders should note the laundering phase is starting, which can keep hardware-wallet security headlines alive without directly moving spot Bitcoin price.
items.impact: Sentiment drag on self-custody narrative, limited immediate price impact

items.title: Strong August NFP Lifts Fed Hike Odds to ~60%
items.summary: US nonfarm payrolls surged 162,000 in August, far above the 50-56,000 expected, with unemployment steady at 4.1 percent and prior months revised higher. Wage growth slowed to 3.1 percent year-on-year. This keeps the labor market solid and raises September FOMC rate-hike odds to around 58-60 percent from about 50 percent, putting pressure on risk assets ahead of this week's inflation data. Crypto traders should watch because higher-for-longer rates typically tighten liquidity and weigh on Bitcoin.
items.impact: Raises odds of tighter Fed policy, pressuring risk assets and BTC

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Tests 4.8% Amid Fiscal Worries
items.summary: The US 10-year yield closed near 4.78 percent after the jobs data and remains under pressure from heavy debt issuance, deficits over 40 trillion dollars, and inflation risks from oil. Analysts flag a sustained break above 4.8 percent as potentially disruptive for other assets. Long-end yields have climbed on structural fiscal concerns even as short rates price modest hikes. This matters for crypto because elevated real yields compete with non-yielding assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Higher yields tighten financial conditions and hurt valuations

items.title: Dollar Strengthens Post-NFP, Tests 200-Day Average
items.summary: The US dollar index pushed higher after the strong jobs report, trading near 99.15-99.18 and testing its 200-day moving average around 99.15 before some consolidation into the holiday. Markets are pricing more Fed tightening support for the greenback. Thin Labor Day trading kept moves contained. A firmer dollar is typically a headwind for Bitcoin and other risk assets priced in USD.
items.impact: Stronger DXY acts as liquidity drain for crypto and EM assets

items.title: Eurozone Q2 GDP Revised Sharply Higher to 0.6%
items.summary: Eurostat's third estimate lifted euro area Q2 GDP growth to 0.6 percent quarter-on-quarter from 0.4 percent, and 1.2 percent year-on-year, with the EU even stronger at 0.7 percent QoQ. Net trade and consumption drove the upgrade. This shows resilience despite energy shocks and supports the case for an ECB hike this week. Stronger European growth is modestly positive for global risk sentiment but also keeps central banks vigilant on inflation.
items.impact: Supports ECB hawkishness while aiding global growth narrative

items.title: CPI and PPI This Week Critical for September FOMC
items.summary: No major US data today due to Labor Day, but August PPI arrives Thursday and CPI Friday, just days before the September 15-16 FOMC. Markets expect a pickup in monthly CPI after a soft July, and the prints will decide whether the Fed hikes from the current 3.50-3.75 percent range. Dovish comments from some officials leave the decision finely balanced. Crypto traders need to position carefully as a hot print would cement hike bets and spike volatility.
items.impact: Binary catalyst for rate path and risk appetite this week

items.title: ECB Widely Expected to Hike Rates on Thursday
items.summary: Markets fully price a 25-basis-point ECB deposit rate rise to 2.50 percent this Thursday as energy prices from Middle East tensions push eurozone inflation back above 3 percent. Focus will be on guidance for further moves and new projections. The hike is seen as insurance against second-round effects. This keeps global policy tighter and may support the euro while adding to the higher-rates backdrop for crypto.
items.impact: Adds to global tightening impulse and inflation vigilance

items.title: Iran Plans Hormuz Exclusion Zone After US Tanker Strikes
items.summary: Over the weekend the US struck three Iranian oil tankers after Iran fired ballistic missiles at American warships near the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran responded by announcing it will declare a new restricted zone outside the strait in the coming days, sanctioning any ship that enters, while oil prices climbed with Brent near 96 dollars and WTI around 92. This keeps the energy chokepoint under threat and raises the odds of prolonged supply disruptions. Traders should care because higher oil feeds inflation fears, tighter financial conditions, and classic risk-off pressure on Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: Elevated oil and ME risk premium pressure risk assets

items.title: Far-Right AfD Wins Historic Saxony-Anhalt Election
items.summary: Germany's Alternative for Germany party scored a landslide 43.8 percent in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, more than doubling its prior result and finishing far ahead of the CDU. It fell just short of an absolute majority with 39 of 83 seats, leaving coalition talks messy because mainstream parties maintain a firewall against it. European leaders called the outcome worrying. For markets this signals deepening political fragmentation in Europe's largest economy and potential policy uncertainty ahead of bigger contests.
items.impact: EU political risk rises but no immediate policy shift

items.title: Canada Retaliatory Tariffs Hit US Goods Starting Tuesday
items.summary: Canada's counter-tariffs of up to 50 percent on roughly 20 to 27 billion dollars of US goods take effect September 8, matching Trump administration levies dollar-for-dollar after talks collapsed. Targets include steel, aluminum, dairy, appliances, electronics and more. Trump has already threatened further escalation. This deepens the North American trade war, raises costs for businesses on both sides, and adds another headwind to growth just as midterms approach.
items.impact: Trade-war drag on growth and risk sentiment

items.title: US Envoys Meet Zelensky After Putin; No Peace Breakthrough
items.summary: Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held their first Kyiv talks with President Zelensky on Sunday after meeting Putin in Moscow. Both sides called the discussions substantive and expressed hope for renewed trilateral talks, yet no ceasefire or territorial deal emerged. Zelensky warned the war is likely to continue into winter and pressed for more air defenses and energy support. Status-quo fighting means ongoing uncertainty for energy, grain, and European risk assets.
items.impact: War continues; limited near-term de-escalation catalyst

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill 11 in Southern Lebanon Including Children
items.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit a residential building and a vehicle in Kfar Reman early Monday, killing at least eleven people including two children and two medics, according to Lebanese officials. This follows Sunday strikes that killed seven and comes after Israel seized a strategic ridge near Nabatieh. Lebanon's president called it a dangerous escalation jeopardizing the US-brokered ceasefire with Hezbollah. Fresh Middle East fighting keeps the regional risk premium elevated alongside the Iran conflict.
items.impact: Adds to ME instability and risk-off pressure

items.title: Oil Nears Multi-Month Highs on Prolonged Hormuz Fears
items.summary: Crude extended gains Monday with WTI near 92 dollars and Brent around 96 to 97 as markets priced in the weekend US-Iran tanker exchanges and Iran's planned restricted zone. Transits through Hormuz remain depressed and US officials say they are strangling Iran's economy while keeping naval escorts active. Sustained high energy prices raise the chance of stickier inflation and tighter policy expectations. Crypto traders watch this closely because oil spikes have repeatedly correlated with risk-asset drawdowns.
items.impact: Higher energy costs threaten liquidity and risk appetite
